about: Name inventory proposed from reference/upstream (see SOURCES.md). Names only; no code. Paths in sources are relative to reference/.

naming_questions.question: NetworkConnect/NetworkDisconnect: add a standalone `docker_network_attachment` resource (container x network pair), or make docker_container `networks` connect/disconnect in place instead of forcing replacement? (or both, with a conflict warning)
Build cache prune action name: `docker_builder_prune` (matches `docker builder prune`) or `docker_build_cache_prune` (avoids confusion with docker_buildx_builder)?
Standalone build: add an action `docker_image_build`, or keep builds only in docker_image's `build` block? If added, is the name too close to docker_image?

Managing an already-joined swarm node (labels/availability/role via NodeUpdate) that Terraform did not join: extend docker_swarm_node with an adopt mode, or add a separate `docker_node` resource (name matches existing data.docker_node)?
Node role actions: `docker_node_promote` / `docker_node_demote` (CLI words, matching docker_node_drain/activate) or one `docker_node_role` action with role = manager|worker?
Logs: separate `docker_service_logs` and `docker_task_logs` data sources, or extend data.docker_logs with service_id / task_id arguments?
SystemAuth (/auth) returns an identity token: model as an ephemeral resource (e.g. `docker_registry_login`) next to ephemeral docker_registry_token, or skip it?
PluginCreate: action `docker_plugin_create` (one-shot) or a resource (it has PluginDelete) with a different name to avoid confusion with docker_plugin (install from registry)?
Container one-off read of files: data source `docker_container_file` (GET archive) vs an action; and copy-in at any time: action `docker_container_upload` or `docker_container_cp`?

Swarm rotation actions: separate `docker_swarm_rotate_unlock_key` and `docker_swarm_ca_rotate`, or one `docker_swarm_rotate` action with what = worker_token|manager_token|unlock_key|ca (absorbing docker_swarm_rotate_tokens)?
Imperative compose actions beside the docker_compose resource: name them docker_compose_up/down (CLI-shaped), docker_compose_apply/destroy, or skip up/down since the resource covers them?

`compose config` render: data source docker_compose_config (visually collides with docker_config and top-level `configs`), docker_compose_project / docker_compose_model, or a provider function compose_render?
`compose ps` / `compose ls`: docker_compose_ps + docker_compose_ls (CLI names) or docker_compose_containers + docker_compose_projects (noun convention like docker_containers)?
`compose volumes`: add a docker_compose_volumes data source, or document data.docker_volume/list.docker_volume with a project label filter (avoids the docker_volume clash)?
Per-container verbs (start/stop/restart/kill/pause/unpause): separate docker_compose_* actions, or one set of docker_container_* actions with an optional project/service selector?
`compose scale` vs existing docker_service_scale: new docker_compose_scale action, or extend docker_service_scale to compose local projects?
Compose top-level elements: keep all inside docker_compose, or split docker_compose_service/network/volume (confusable with docker_service/docker_network/docker_volume)?
jobs: support in docker_compose (run once on apply) plus docker_compose_run for manual triggers, or leave unsupported but add a warning?

Manifest lists: `docker_registry_manifest_list` (proposed, registry family) vs `docker_manifest_list` vs `docker_buildx_imagetools`? One resource for both `docker manifest create/push` and `buildx imagetools create`.
BuildKit build: keep extending `docker_image` (build block) vs add `docker_buildx_build`? Proposed: extend docker_image, and add action `docker_buildx_bake` for multi-target / non-image outputs.

Stack: keep existing `docker_stack` vs a `docker_swarm_stack` prefix for consistency with docker_swarm_*? Proposed: keep docker_stack; new stack data sources `docker_stacks` and `docker_stack` (or `docker_stack_services`).

Context: skip `docker_context` (provider `context`/`host` arguments already select the daemon) vs a read-only `docker_context` data source that resolves a context's endpoint/TLS from ~/.docker? Proposed: skip.
Build cache prune: one action for both daemon build cache (POST /build/prune, Z1) and buildx builders (BuildKit gRPC): `docker_buildx_prune` vs `docker_build_cache_prune` vs `docker_builder_prune`?

Buildx builder data sources: `docker_buildx_builder` (singular, same name as the resource) + `docker_buildx_builders`; buildx history as `docker_buildx_history` (+ `docker_buildx_history_record`) or one data source with an optional ref?
docker buildx stop: action `docker_buildx_builder_stop` or skip (low value)?
Disk usage: `docker_buildx_disk_usage` separate from Z1's system df data source, or one data source with an optional builder?

Shape: (a) one type per instruction (docker_dockerfile_run, docker_dockerfile_from, ...) vs (b) a single data source data.docker_dockerfile with ordered nested blocks (stage { from, run, copy ... }) rendering Dockerfile text vs (c) a provider function. (b) recommended: ordering and stages fit nested blocks; 21 trivial types would bloat the registry.
Directives: docker_dockerfile_directive_syntax/escape/check types vs top-level attributes syntax, escape, check { skip = [...], error = bool } on data.docker_dockerfile (recommended).
Include MAINTAINER (deprecated) at all, or omit and steer users to LABEL org.opencontainers.image.authors?
ONBUILD: separate block nesting an instruction vs an `onbuild = true` attribute on each instruction block?
Stages: model FROM ... AS name as a `stage` block with `name` (recommended) rather than a FROM flag?
check rule names: validate against a pinned list (21 rules at frontend 1.28) or accept free strings?

Z1: Coverage self-check: 108 operations, 108 covered, 0 uncovered (each with exactly one `primary: true` swagger source); duplicates-as-primary: 0; unknown operationIds: 0.

Source: upstream/engine-api/api/swagger.yaml (Engine API 1.56), parsed with PyYAML; 108 operations across tags Container, Image, System, Exec, Volume, Network, Plugin, Node, Swarm, Service, Task, Secret, Config, Distribution, Session.

Schema extension: swagger source entries carry `primary: true` on the one item that is the operation's home; other items that also use the op list it without `primary` (e.g. ContainerInspect in docker_container resource vs data source, SwarmUpdate in rotate actions). Swagger sources also carry `min_api` where the CHANGELOG states the endpoint was added.

min_api: the swagger descriptions carry no version text (only Session's deprecation). Values come from upstream/engine-api/api/docs/CHANGELOG.md endpoint-added lines: archive 1.20, volumes 1.21, container update 1.22, prune/plugins/secrets 1.25, plugin upgrade 1.26, distribution 1.30, session 1.31, VolumeUpdate 1.42, image attestations 1.55, _ping GET 1.11 / HEAD 1.40. Swarm/node/service/task/config/network/exec/image core endpoints predate CHANGELOG 'added' lines: null. Item-level min_api is the stated min of the item's create/primary op.

Status was judged by grepping internal/provider/*.go (non-test) for moby client calls: unused in provider code are ContainerStop/Restart/Kill/Pause/Unpause/Wait/Top/Stats/Diff/Commit/StatPath/CopyFromContainer, ImageHistory/Search/Attestations, NetworkDisconnect, VolumeUpdate, PluginUpgrade/Push/Create/List, SwarmUnlock, SecretUpdate, ConfigUpdate, TaskInspect, Service/Task logs, Events, DiskUsage, RegistryLogin(/auth).
docker_system_prune covers ContainerPrune, NetworkPrune, VolumePrune and BuildPrune through boolean switches, so the dedicated per-kind prune actions are marked partial rather than missing.
client.PluginInstall calls GetPluginPrivileges + PluginPull, client.ImagePull calls ImageCreate; both counted as used by the existing resources.
docker_stack, docker_compose and compose2stack have no Engine endpoint of their own (client-side); out of scope for this engine lane.
ImageDelete is shared by docker_image (primary) and docker_tag (untag on destroy).
Z2: All CLI items are client-side (cli_only=true): `docker compose` composes Engine API calls selected by com.docker.compose.* labels; summaries name the calls.

The provider pins compose-go v2.16.2. Its embedded schema (upstream/compose-spec/compose-go-embedded.json) differs from compose-spec main only in: container_spec mem_limit, memswap_limit, shm_size typed number|string (spec: integer|string), and no jobs.*.extends (Compose NEXT). It already has jobs, models, include, schedule.
Spec items handled by docker_compose use name docker_compose (kind resource) rather than inventing per-element types; splitting is a naming question.
docker_compose silently ignores top-level jobs (no warning) and warns on models; worth a TODO even without new types.
docker_stack is HCL-native (service blocks), not compose-file driven; docker_compose mode=swarm is the compose-file path to a stack. tools/compose2stack is a one-shot converter, not a Terraform type.
compose_convert has only a yaml (no .md) in compose-cli v5.1.4 docs; it is an alias of config. docker_compose.yaml is the root command.
climap compose rows: up, down, ps, up --scale -> docker_compose; exec -> docker_exec; logs -> docker_logs; pull -> docker_image; config/convert -> tools/compose2stack; build, run/watch/alpha -> none.
Z3: Scope: docker CLI 29.5.3 docs (commandline/*.md + docker-trust plugin docs), buildx v0.38.2 docs, CLI plugins seen in the Docker Desktop 4.78 help capture. Compose plugin is another lane.
Items exist only for commands with no Engine API endpoint (or whose Engine endpoint covers only a minor part: login). Every other core command is handled_by "engine" in z3-cli-map.json for lane Z1.

buildx create/rm are grouped into one resource item (schema rule: one resource per object); other buildx commands get one item each. Group pages (buildx, history, imagetools, policy, dap, debug, replay) are folded into their children's sources.
Buildx commands newer than the installed v0.34.1 (docs present, help absent): buildx debug, debug build, policy json-schema, replay, replay build. `history trace` is in both.

cli_only=true marks client-side/BuildKit/registry/plugin work. Items whose `channel` field mentions BuildKit talk gRPC to the builder (with the docker driver, through POST /session + the undocumented /grpc upgrade), not the documented Engine API.
manifest list proposal reuses the docker_registry_* family (registry API v2), not docker_buildx_* or docker_manifest_*.
Help capture was taken on a non-swarm Docker Desktop: swarm-only commands are missing from help for environmental reasons (see z3-cli-map.json summary).
Z4: Source: Dockerfile frontend 1.28.0 reference.md. syntax.md and experimental.md are redirect stubs ('This page has moved to reference.md'); no labs-only instructions or flags are documented in this snapshot, so no flag carries "labs": true.

min_syntax comes from the 'Minimum Dockerfile version' tables (RUN, ADD, COPY) and inline 'since Dockerfile v1.x' text; blank table cells (COPY --from, COPY/ADD --chown) get no min_syntax. Sub-option versions (secret env 1.10, chmod symbolic 1.14, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH 1.5) are noted inside options.
RUN --device also needs BuildKit 0.20.0; HEALTHCHECK --start-interval needs Docker Engine 25.0; RUN --network=host, --security=insecure and --device need buildkitd entitlements (noted on the flag).
Shell form, exec form and heredoc are flag entries on the instructions that accept them; heredocs are documented for RUN and COPY only.
check directive flags = skip, error, then one flag per build-check rule (21 rules from rules/*.md; InvalidDefinitionDescription is experimental). Rule anchors are rules/<file>.md paths.
MAINTAINER kept as a dockerfile_block (not skip): it still parses in 1.28 and appears in existing Dockerfiles; status_note marks it deprecated.
Not itemised: .dockerignore (context-side file, not an instruction), environment replacement rules (cross-cutting syntax), comments.
All '#' anchors verified against GitHub-style slugs of reference.md headings by z4_gen.py; rules files verified to exist.

Status 'missing' for every block: the provider has no Dockerfile composer. Related: docker_image (resource) build block takes context + dockerfile path and builds via the Engine API / BuildKit session.

items.name: docker_container
items.summary: Container lifecycle: create (+connect networks, upload files), start, in-place update of resources/restart policy and rename, remove.
items.status_note: Covers ContainerCreate/Update/Rename/Delete; PutContainerArchive only through `upload` blocks before first start; networks connected only at create (NetworkConnect), never connected/disconnected in place.

items.name: docker_image
items.summary: Local image: pull (ImageCreate fromImage) or build, inspect, remove.
items.status_note: ImageCreate fromSrc (import) lives in action docker_image_import.

items.name: docker_network
items.summary: Network: create, inspect, remove (all settings force replacement).

items.name: docker_network_attachment
items.summary: Connect an existing container to a network (create) and disconnect it (destroy), independent of the container's lifecycle.
items.status_note: docker_container connects its `networks` at create only; NetworkDisconnect is never called and there is no standalone attachment.
items.collision: Overlaps docker_container `networks`; managing the same pair in both would fight.

items.name: docker_plugin

items.status_note: PluginUpgrade (1.26) is never used: a changed remote reference forces replacement instead of an in-place upgrade.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: configs: file/environment/content-sourced config objects; copied into containers locally, created as Swarm configs in swarm mode.
items.status_note: Local mode copies the content into the container (no bind mount); swarm mode creates Swarm configs but ignores driver and template_driver with a warning.
items.collision: Top-level `configs` vs docker_config (Swarm config resource) vs the proposed docker_compose_config data source (CLI `compose config`, rendered model).

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: include: pull other compose files (with own project_directory/env_file) into the model.
items.status_note: Local-path includes are resolved by the compose-go loader; remote (git/oci) includes are disabled by design (compose_parse.go).

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: jobs: run-to-completion containers with manual or scheduled triggers (Compose NEXT).
items.status_note: compose-go v2.16.2 parses jobs (Project.Jobs) but docker_compose never reads them: silently ignored, not even warned. Scheduled triggers need a scheduler outside Terraform; manual runs map to the proposed docker_compose_run action. The embedded compose-go schema lacks jobs.*.extends.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: models: AI models (Docker Model Runner) that services bind to via endpoint/model env vars.
items.status_note: Parsed by compose-go but ignored: service `models` gets a warning in local mode; the top-level element is never acted on. Model Runner is not part of the Docker Engine API, so support needs a separate client.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: name: project name used to prefix and label every object.
items.status_note: docker_compose.project_name defaults to the file's top-level name.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: networks: project networks created and labelled by docker_compose (bridge locally, overlay in swarm); external networks are referenced only.
items.collision: docker_compose_network would be confusable with docker_network.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: secrets: file/environment-sourced secrets; copied to /run/secrets locally, created as Swarm secrets in swarm mode.
items.status_note: Local mode copies content into the container (no bind mount as compose does); swarm mode ignores driver and template_driver with a warning.
items.collision: docker_compose_secret would be confusable with docker_secret.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: services: long-running containers (local) or Swarm services (swarm), managed as part of the docker_compose project.
items.status_note: docker_compose loads services with compose-go and creates containers (local) or Swarm services (swarm). Ignored with a warning: build (no image is an error, pull_policy build errors), develop, pre_start/post_start/pre_stop hooks, models, provider, credential_spec, blkio_config, use_api_socket, external_links, attach (local); swarm mode also ignores container_name, depends_on, network_mode, privileged, devices, ipc/pid/userns/uts/cgroup_parent, security_opt, shm_size, volumes_from, gpus, links, tmpfs, pull_policy other than missing/always.
items.collision: A per-service type named docker_compose_service would be confusable with docker_service (swarm). Keep services inside docker_compose.

items.name: docker_compose
items.summary: volumes: named project volumes created by docker_compose (removed on destroy unless keep_volumes); external volumes referenced only.
items.collision: docker_compose_volume(s) would be confusable with docker_volume and with the proposed docker_compose_volumes data source (CLI `compose volumes`).

items.name: docker_image
items.summary: service.build: build the service image (context, dockerfile, args, secrets, cache, platforms...).
items.status_note: docker_compose does not build (warns; errors when image is unset); docker_image covers the build as a separate resource. A build action would be docker_compose_build.

items.name: docker_service
items.summary: service.deploy: replicas, mode, resources, restart/update/rollback policy, placement, labels.
items.status_note: docker_compose swarm mode maps deploy to the Swarm service spec; local mode uses replicas (scale), global mode and resources. Not its own Terraform type: it is the docker_service spec.

items.name: docker_compose_config
items.summary: Parse, interpolate, merge and render the compose model in canonical form (no Engine call).
items.status_note: tools/compose2stack converts once at authoring time (a tool, not a type); compose_env only builds env. No type renders the model.
items.collision: Confusable with top-level compose `configs` and docker_config (swarm config resource). Alternatives: docker_compose_project, docker_compose_model, or function compose_render.

items.name: docker_buildx_builder
items.summary: docker buildx create / rm: create and remove a BuildKit builder instance.
items.status_note: Only the docker-container driver, single node: no kubernetes/remote/cloud drivers, no --append/--node/--leave multi-node builders, no --platform pinning per node, no --driver-opt beyond image/network/env/restart/memory etc. Builder is a container + state volume created via Engine API; buildx's local store (~/.docker/buildx/instances) is not written, so `docker buildx ls` will not list it.
items.channel: Engine API for the docker-container driver's container/volume; BuildKit gRPC for bootstrap/workers

items.name: docker_image
items.summary: docker buildx build: build with BuildKit (multi-platform, exporters, cache import/export, secrets, ssh, attestations).
items.status_note: docker_image.build has context, dockerfile, target, args, labels, platform(s), pull, no_cache, cache_from, secrets, builder. Missing: --output/exporters (local, tar, oci, registry with push), --cache-to, --ssh, --attest/--sbom/--provenance, --annotation, --network, --add-host, --build-context (named contexts), --shm-size, --ulimit, --call/--check, --iidfile/metadata, --policy (0.38).
items.collision: Do not add docker_buildx_build: it would duplicate docker_image. If exporters that produce no local image are wanted, that is an action (docker_buildx_bake or docker_image_build action), not a second build resource.

items.name: docker_buildx_bake
items.summary: docker buildx bake / docker bake: build one or more targets from a bake file (HCL/JSON/compose) in one BuildKit session.
items.collision: Overlaps docker_image (build block) for single targets.
items.design_note: Action, not resource: bake outputs are often not local images (registry push, local/tar exporters) and the target set is chosen per run. The action takes either a bake file path + target names, or inline `target` blocks mirroring bake's target attributes; Terraform variables/for_each replace bake variables/groups/matrix. Images that Terraform should own stay docker_image.

items.summary: docker buildx stop: stop a builder's BuildKit node (the buildx_buildkit_* container) without removing it.

items.channel: For the docker-container driver this is Engine ContainerStop; for remote drivers there is nothing to stop.

items.summary: docker buildx prune: remove build cache on a builder (filters, keep-storage/min-free-space, --all).
items.status_note: docker_system_prune can include the daemon's build cache (POST /build/prune) for the built-in builder only; nothing prunes a docker-container builder's cache.
items.collision: Z1 will likely propose an Engine action for POST /build/prune (e.g. docker_build_cache_prune / docker_builder_prune). One type should take an optional `builder` and choose BuildKit gRPC vs POST /build/prune.
items.channel: BuildKit gRPC/session, not Engine API (docker driver falls back to POST /build/prune)

items.summary: Bake `function` blocks and the bake standard library (go-cty functions, mostly the same set Terraform has).
items.skip_reason: Bake HCL is itself HCL built on the same go-cty stdlib; Terraform functions (plus provider functions) replace user functions.

items.summary: Bake `group` block: a named set of targets built together.
items.skip_reason: A list of target names; in Terraform this is the docker_buildx_bake action's `targets` argument or a for_each over targets.

items.summary: Bake `target` block: one build (context, dockerfile, args, tags, platforms, cache-from/to, output, secret, ssh, attest, matrix, inherits, call, entitlements, policy...).
items.skip_reason: Not a Terraform type: becomes a nested `target` block of the docker_buildx_bake action (and its attributes mirror docker_image.build). `inherits` and `matrix` map to Terraform locals/for_each.

items.summary: Bake `variable` block: typed, overridable inputs with env-var defaults.
items.skip_reason: Terraform variables/locals replace them; when the action consumes an existing bake file, overrides go through a `set`/`variables` map argument.

items.summary: docker buildx dap build: run a build under a Debug Adapter Protocol debugger.
items.skip_reason: Interactive IDE debugging session; not declarative.

items.summary: docker buildx debug build: interactive debug shell on build failure (experimental).
items.skip_reason: Experimental, interactive; also newer than the installed buildx v0.34.1 (not in help capture).

items.summary: docker buildx dial-stdio: proxy the BuildKit API over stdio.
items.skip_reason: Transport plumbing for other tools; the provider dials BuildKit directly.

items.summary: docker buildx history export.
items.skip_reason: Exports a Docker Desktop .dockerbuild bundle (Desktop UI artifact).

items.summary: docker buildx history import.
items.skip_reason: Imports a Docker Desktop .dockerbuild bundle (Desktop UI artifact).

items.summary: docker buildx history inspect attachment.
items.skip_reason: Returns raw attachment blobs (SBOM/provenance) of a record; low value as state, and docker_image attestations are Z1's ImageAttestations territory.

items.summary: docker buildx history logs.
items.skip_reason: Build log stream; logs are not Terraform state.

items.summary: docker buildx history open.
items.skip_reason: Opens the Docker Desktop UI.

items.summary: docker buildx history rm.
items.skip_reason: Deleting build records is housekeeping; covered well enough by buildx prune / builder recreation. Revisit as an action if asked.

items.summary: docker buildx history trace.
items.skip_reason: Starts a local Jaeger UI for the trace; interactive.

items.summary: docker buildx imagetools create: create/push a manifest list or index from existing images (with annotations), server-side copy.
items.skip_reason: Same object as cli-only:manifest-list (proposed docker_registry_manifest_list); one resource covers both `docker manifest create/push` and imagetools create.
items.collision: docker_buildx_imagetools_create would duplicate docker_registry_manifest_list.

items.summary: docker buildx policy eval.
items.skip_reason: Build-policy (Rego) development tooling, client-local; build policy itself is a --policy input on build/bake.

items.summary: docker buildx policy json-schema.
items.skip_reason: Prints a JSON schema; newer than installed buildx v0.34.1.

items.summary: docker buildx policy test.
items.skip_reason: Build-policy (Rego) development tooling, client-local.

items.summary: docker buildx replay build: rebuild an image from its provenance attestation and pinned materials (new in buildx 0.38).
items.skip_reason: New and experimental reproducibility tooling, newer than installed buildx v0.34.1; revisit as an action docker_buildx_replay once stable.

items.summary: docker buildx use: set the current builder in the client's buildx config.
items.skip_reason: Client-side default selection; Terraform references the builder explicitly via docker_image.build.builder.

items.summary: docker buildx version.
items.skip_reason: Client version print.

items.name: docker_registry_manifest_list
items.summary: Build a manifest list / OCI index from existing per-platform images in a registry, annotate entries (os/arch/variant/features) and push it under a tag; delete the tag on destroy.
items.status_note: docker_registry_image pushes single images; nothing assembles an index from existing digests.
items.collision: Same job as `docker buildx imagetools create` (buildx:imagetools-create points here). Do not also add docker_buildx_imagetools / docker_manifest. `docker manifest rm` only deletes the local draft, so destroy semantics (registry DELETE of the tag vs leave it) need a flag like docker_registry_image.keep_remotely.
items.implementation_note: Registry HTTP API v2 (distribution), not Engine API; the provider already has registry auth + manifest fetch code for docker_registry_image_manifests.

items.name: docker_stack
items.summary: docker stack deploy / rm: client-side fan-out of a compose file into namespaced networks, secrets, configs and services (label com.docker.stack.namespace).
items.collision: Keep `docker_stack` (exists); do not rename to docker_swarm_stack even though it is a swarm-layer type.
items.stack_deploy_flags_note: --prune, --resolve-image and --with-registry-auth should be checked against docker_stack attributes by the implementing lane.

items.name: docker_registry_image_manifests
items.summary: docker manifest inspect: read an image manifest or manifest list straight from the registry.
items.collision: buildx:imagetools-inspect maps to the same data source.

items.name: docker_stack
items.summary: docker stack services: the services of one stack (GET /services filtered by namespace label), with replica counts from tasks.
items.status_note: docker_services + label filter covers the list; running/desired replica counts (from tasks) are missing.
items.collision: Data source `docker_stack` would share its name with the existing docker_stack resource (allowed by Terraform, same pattern as docker_image); alternative name docker_stack_services.

items.name: docker_stacks
items.summary: docker stack ls: stacks derived by grouping services by the com.docker.stack.namespace label (name, service count).
items.status_note: docker_services with a label filter returns the services but not the grouped stack list.

items.summary: docker checkpoint create/ls/rm: CRIU checkpoint of a running container (experimental).
items.skip_reason: Experimental (needs experimental daemon + CRIU, Linux only); daemon endpoints /containers/{id}/checkpoints exist but are undocumented and absent from swagger.yaml 1.56. Revisit only if moby documents them (then: action docker_container_checkpoint).

items.summary: docker context create/update/rm/use/show/ls/inspect/export/import: named daemon endpoints stored in ~/.docker/contexts.
items.skip_reason: Client-side config store, no Engine API; the provider's `context`, `host`, `tls` and `ssh` arguments already select the daemon, and writing files under ~/.docker from Terraform would be a local-file side effect.
items.collision: A `docker_context` resource would be confusable with the provider-level `context` argument.

items.summary: docker login: validate registry credentials (POST /auth) and store them in config.json or a credential helper.
items.skip_reason: Only the validation half is Engine API (POST /auth, which Z1 owns); persisting credentials is client config. Terraform supplies credentials per run via provider registry_auth (password_wo) and ephemeral docker_registry_token.

items.summary: docker logout: remove stored registry credentials from config.json / credential helper.
items.skip_reason: Pure client config edit, no endpoint; Terraform never persists credentials, so there is nothing to log out of.

items.summary: docker stack config: print the merged, interpolated compose file a stack deploy would use.
items.skip_reason: Pure client-side compose rendering with no daemon call; covered by tools/compose2stack and the compose lane.

items.summary: docker stack ps: tasks of a stack (GET /tasks filtered by namespace label).
items.skip_reason: Same as the tasks list data source Z1 derives from GET /tasks with a label filter (com.docker.stack.namespace); no separate type.

items.summary: docker system dial-stdio: proxy stdio to the daemon socket (used by ssh:// connections).
items.skip_reason: Transport plumbing for the CLI's ssh:// helper; the provider's ssh block is pure Go and does not need it.

items.summary: docker trust inspect/sign/revoke/key generate|load/signer add|remove: Docker Content Trust (Notary v1) signing.
items.skip_reason: Notary v1 client against a Notary server, no Engine API; split out of docker/cli into the docker-trust plugin and DCT is being retired by Docker Hub. Signing belongs to cosign/notation-style providers.

items.summary: Docker AI Agent Runner (docker-agent): run, share and serve AI agents.
items.skip_reason: Docker Desktop AI product plugin; talks to model providers and its own runtime, not the Engine API.

items.summary: Ask Gordon: Docker Desktop AI assistant.
items.skip_reason: Interactive Docker Desktop product feature; no Engine API.

items.summary: docker debug: shell into any image or container with a toolbox.
items.skip_reason: Docker Desktop (Pro) plugin; composite of Engine calls (create helper container, exec) plus proprietary toolbox; interactive. docker_exec covers the declarative part.

items.summary: Docker Desktop control (start/stop/restart, engine, kubernetes, update, logs, diagnose).
items.skip_reason: Controls the Docker Desktop app via its backend socket, not the Engine API.

items.summary: Docker Hardened Images catalog, mirror, auth, attestations.
items.skip_reason: Docker Hub product API (DHI), not Engine API; mirroring could later be a registry-side resource in a Hub provider.

items.summary: Docker Desktop extensions install/ls/rm/update/dev/validate.
items.skip_reason: Docker Desktop extension manager; not Engine API.

items.summary: docker init: generate Dockerfile, compose.yaml and .dockerignore starter files.
items.skip_reason: Interactive local file scaffolding; no daemon involved.

items.summary: Docker MCP Toolkit: catalog, gateway, servers, secrets, OAuth, profiles.
items.skip_reason: Docker Desktop MCP product; own gateway/catalog APIs, not Engine API (gateway runs MCP servers as containers through Docker but via its own logic).

items.summary: Docker Model Runner: pull/run/list/package/push models, runner install/start/stop.
items.skip_reason: Model Runner has its own HTTP API (OpenAI-compatible, /models, /engines via the Desktop socket or localhost:12434, or a docker/model-runner container on plain Engine), not the Engine API. Plausible future provider surface (docker_model resource for pull/rm, install-runner as a container), but it is a separate API; out of scope for Engine-API parity.

items.summary: Docker Offload: run builds/containers on Docker cloud.
items.skip_reason: Docker cloud product session; not Engine API (it switches the daemon endpoint).

items.summary: Docker Pass secrets manager (beta): get/set/ls/rm secrets, run with secrets.
items.skip_reason: Local/Desktop secrets store; Terraform has its own secret handling (write-only args, ephemeral).

items.summary: Docker Sandboxes: microVM sandboxes for coding agents (create, exec, run, network, save).
items.skip_reason: Docker Desktop sandbox product with its own VM backend API, not Engine API.

items.summary: Docker Scout: CVEs, SBOM, policy, recommendations, compare, repo enrollment.
items.skip_reason: Docker Scout SaaS/analysis tool; not Engine API. Vulnerability data could later be a data source in a Scout/Hub provider.

notes: handled_by: engine = has a swagger.yaml (API 1.56) endpoint, item made by lane Z1; group = management-command doc page with no operation of its own; cli-only:*/buildx:*/plugin:* = item id in z3-cli.json.

Help capture is from Docker Desktop 4.78 (CLI 29.5.3) with the daemon NOT a swarm manager, so node/service/secret/config/stack and most swarm subcommands are hidden from --help: their absence is environmental, not a docs/CLI mismatch.
checkpoint is experimental (hidden without experimental CLI); trust lives in the separate docker-trust plugin (cmd/docker-trust), not installed; system dial-stdio is hidden.
`docker builder` help resolved to `docker buildx`, so `builder build` / `builder prune` children were not walked.
`docker swarm init --help` resolved to the docker-init plugin (help-capture oddity).
login has POST /auth but it only validates credentials; mapped to item cli-only:login (engine_api kept).
